UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
[PROPOSEDI ORDER B
GRANTING RECONSIDERATION, VACATING ECF NO. 96, RESTORING THE
HISTORICAL REQUEST, AND DIRECTING DEVELOPMENT OF THE
OWNERSHIP RECORD FOR DETERMINATION
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Rule 54(b) Motion to Vacate ECF No. 96 and
Determine Magistrate Judge Davis's Ownership of Meta Common Stock (the "Motion"). Upon
consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, any response and reply, and the record,
including ECF Nos. 64, 84, 86, 86-1 through 86-3, 87, 93, 96, 97, and 99 and the docket entry of
October 22, 2026, it is hereby
ORDERED as follows:
The Motion is GRANTED IN PART as stated in this Order.
The Order entered October 22, 2026 (ECF No. 96) is VACATED under Federal
Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b).
1

3.
The historical financial-interest component of Plaintiff's Motion to Disqualify
(ECF No. 86), identified in Part V and Request A2 of that motion, is RESTORED for decision as
to September 9, 2026 and October 7, 2026.
4.
The question restored for decision is the following, as to each date separately:
whether the asset reported as "FB common stock" at Part VII, line 6, of the
Financial Disclosure Reports at ECF No. 86-2 at 3 (report page 2) and ECF No. 86-3 at 5 (report
page 4) is common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.;
(b)
whether, on September 9, 2026, that asset was owned by Magistrate Judge Ivan
D. Davis individually or as a fiduciary, by his spouse, or by a minor child residing in his household,
and by which;
(C)
whether, on October 7, 2026, that asset was owned by Magistrate Judge Ivan D.
Davis individually or as a fiduciary, by his spouse, or by a minor child residing in his household,
and by which;
(d)
whether, on each of those dates, the interest was a "financial interest" within the
meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4), and whether it was held through a mutual or common
investment fund within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i); and
(e)
the date and manner of any sale, transfer, or other disposition of the asset
necessary to determine ownership on either date.
To decide the question stated in paragraph 4, the Court will obtain, through a
procedure within the Court's authority, a written statement from Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis
addressing the matters in paragraph 4, the records showing ownership of the reported asset on the
two dates, or both. The Court requests that the statement, the records, or both be filed within
2

fourteen (14) days of the date of this Order. The Court may direct that any portion of the
submission be filed under seal, with a notice of filing on the public docket.
Within fourteen (14) days after the submission described in paragraph 5 is filed,
any party may file a response addressing the resulting record. No reply shall be filed without leave
of Court.
Upon the submission and any responses, the Court will determine the question
stated in paragraph 4 on the record and will state its determination in a written order.
Any determination entered under paragraph 7 will be part of the record in this
action. It will not determine knowledge under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4), the application of 28 U.S.C.
§ 455(f), or the relief requested in ECF No. 93, ECF Nos. 89 through 91, or ECF Nos. 97 through
99, which remain pending before the District Judge and are not decided by this Order.
Prospective relief under ECF No. 86, Requests Al, A3, and A4, directed to
Magistrate Judge Davis's further participation in this action, is unnecessary following the
reassignment recorded on October 22, 2026. This paragraph does not dispose of the historical
request restored in paragraph 3.
10.
The restored request will be decided by the undersigned. Nothing in this Order
returns any matter to Magistrate Judge Davis for adjudication. Nothing in this Order treats the
absence of a submission under paragraph 5 as establishing ownership.
Alexandria, Virginia
_, 2026
William E. Fitzpatrick
United States Magistrate Judge
3
